title: Oriented links in the three-sphere and ambient isotopy
statement: Work in the smooth category. Fix the standard orientation of the three-sphere $S^3=\mathbb R^3\cup\{\infty\}$ (one-point compactification of $\mathbb R^3$ with its standard orientation). An **oriented link** is a smooth embedding $L\colon S^1\sqcup\dots\sqcup S^1\to S^3$ of a finite disjoint union of oriented circles; its image is a finite disjoint union of smoothly embedded circles (all links here are finite and tame by this smoothness convention). Two oriented links $L_0,L_1$ are **equivalent** when there is an orientation-preserving ambient isotopy carrying $L_0$ to $L_1$: a smooth map $H\colon S^3\times I\to S^3$ with $H_0=\mathrm{id}_{S^3}$, each $H_t$ a diffeomorphism, and $H_1\circ L_0=L_1$ as maps of oriented $1$-manifolds. The number of components of $L$ is the number of circles in the source.
strategy: Fix once and for all the smooth/tame category, the model $S^3=\mathbb R^3\cup\{\infty\}$ and the orientation; every projection and every Reidemeister move below is read after moving the link off $\infty$ in $\mathbb R^3$. The orientation-preserving clause is exactly what the oriented Reidemeister moves and the oriented closures must preserve.

references.title: Ozsvath, Stipsicz and Szabo, Grid Homology for Knots and Links, AMS Surveys and Monographs 208 (2015); section 2.1 and Appendix B.1, printed pp. 367-372
Queffelec, Reidemeister's theorem using transversality, Bulletin of the Australian Mathematical Society (2024); arXiv:2406.18203v1, sections 2-3
